expect.name: Chiwawa River Road / FR 6200
expect.status: Open to Atkinson Flat Campground (~mile 16); closed to vehicles beyond that point to Trinity Trailhead under USFS order #06-17-07-2026-11 (effective May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027 unless rescinded sooner) after December 2025 storm damage
expect.driveNote: Same access as the Southwest Face route: from Coles Corner on US-2, WA-207 north, then Chiwawa Loop Road and Chiwawa River Road/FR 6200 ~23 mi to Trinity Trailhead. Under the storm-damage closure, park near Atkinson Flat and walk the final ~7 miles each way; while the Little Giant Fire closure (order 06-17-07-2026-40) is in force, September 3 through October 31, 2026 unless lifted sooner, FR 6200 is closed to all entry, so this walk is not open.
expect.seasonalGate: Normally opens as snow clears, typically by June in an average year, once the current storm-damage closure is lifted; the final 12 miles are rough, native-surface road unsuitable for low-clearance vehicles even when open

expect.name: Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 6200)
expect.status: Closed beyond Atkinson Campground due to storm damage as of June 2026 - verify current status with the Wenatchee River Ranger District before approaching via Trinity/Buck Creek Trailhead.
expect.driveNote: From Leavenworth: US-2 west 15 mi to Coles Corner, right on WA-207 north 4.4 mi, then Chiwawa Loop Road/FR 6200 roughly 22-23 miles to Trinity Trailhead (Buck Creek Trail #1513).
expect.seasonalGate: Typically snow-gated in winter/spring; the final ~12 miles is rough gravel/dirt even when open, and high clearance is recommended.

approach.expect: The historic Staircase (North Fork Skokomish) approach has been closed since the 2025 Bear Gulch Fire, and the Duckabush approach described here is cut too: the Home Sweet Home Trail from the Duckabush River Trail junction over First Divide is also closed, with no reopening date on the park's trail-conditions page (updated September 14, 2026), so no open trail reaches First Divide while the closure stands. The Duckabush approach starts at the Duckabush Trailhead via Duckabush Trail #803. The tread starts easy for about 2.4 miles to Little Hump, then climbs the steep, loose-rock switchbacks of Big Hump before mellowing again to the Olympic National Park boundary around mile 6.2-6.7. Continue up the valley past 5 Mile Camp (a popular fishing/camping flat by the river) and 10 Mile Camp (~mile 12), where the trail's grade eases through old-growth forest along the Duckabush River — reliable water the whole way, though treat it. Beyond 10 Mile Camp the trail steepens again through the rougher upper-valley tread toward the Duckabush Camp junction with the O'Neil Pass/North Fork Skokomish Trail; from there it's a tough, sustained climb — the last mile notably steep — up to Marmot Lake (roughly 20-21 miles from the trailhead), a good base camp near Hart Lake (0.9 mi), Lake LaCrosse (1.4 mi), and O'Neil Pass (1.2 mi). From Marmot Lake, drop back to the Home Sweet Home junction and climb the Home Sweet Home Trail over First Divide (4,688 ft) — closed along with the Staircase side while the Bear Gulch Fire closure stands — then leave maintained trail to angle cross-country/climber's-path up open talus and subalpine meadow toward Mount Hopper's basin below the summit rockwall (high point ~6,120 ft). This upper stretch has real route-finding difficulty: numerous gullies and ribs look equally plausible from below, snow can choke the gully well into summer (ice axe advisable), and the final scramble features loose rock underfoot — expect to backtrack if you pick the wrong line. Given the mileage (~29 miles one-way), most parties treat this as a multi-day trip with a camp at Marmot Lake or Home Sweet Home rather than a car-to-car push.
